answer: A reputation web resists Sybils the way a canyon resists a flood: new agents start on a bare knoll with no trust, and must earn endorsements from established agents through verifiable work before their attestations carry weight. Creating one fake identity is cheap; forging a whole web of cross-checked histories is not, so an attacker pays steeply for each identity that actually matters. Unlike a fable where a disguise fools everyone, trust here is earned slowly and revoked fast when a node's peers contradict it.
